dialogue.agent: Hello, how may I help you today?

dialogue.user: I'm looking for a new pair of shoes. My budget is between $200 and $500, and I'm really focused on quality. I'd like something with an average rating of at least 4.5 out of 5 stars. I'm not too concerned with reviews themselves, just the overall rating. What do you have that fits that description?
dialogue.agent:
Here are some options that fit your criteria:

*   **Moloā - Ray / Toffee Ray / Toffee / 16** - $249.92, 4.8/5 stars, 1 review
*   **Nike Mens Kobe A.D. NXT Basketball Shoes** - $419.00, 4.7/5 stars, 5 reviews. This shoe features an adjustable toggle system, Zoom Air technology, heel-to-toe Lunarlon foam, mesh inner sleeve, and a micro-tread pattern on the outsole for extra traction.

Do any of these catch your eye?

products.title: Justin Boots Men's Performance Ropers Equestrian Boot
products.description: The Standard of the West Since 1879 The story of Justin Boots began in 1879, when H.J. Justin moved to Spanish Fort, Texas to become a boot repairman. He was a quick study, with an eye and talent for boot making. H.J. soon began his own boot company, Justin Boots, which he operated out of his home to serve cowboys passing though town. H.J. saw the potential for his business, so when a railroad was built ten years later in Nocona, Texas, he moved his family there to capitalize on a bigger market. In 1908, Justin Boots became a true family company when his sons, Earl and Avis, came to work for their father. Their combined efforts pushed the company forward, and just two years later, Justin Boots had doubled its production and was being sold in 26 states as well as Mexico, Canada, and Cuba. Seven years after their fathers death in 1918, his sons moved the company headquarters to Fort Worth where it still operates today. Every pair of Justin Boots is a salute to the spirit of independence, hard work and authenticity of the cowboys who have worn them since 1879. After more than 130 years of Western boot making, Justin Boots is still true to its roots. When you purchase a pair of Justin Boots you will own the most authentic and stylish Western footwear available. And with Justins patented J-Flex Comfort System you will be wearing the most comfortable boots ever made. This is why Justin Boots has been crowned the .Standard Of The West Since 1879..

dialogue.user: Hmm, I'm a little hesitant about shoes that are primarily mesh for durability, especially given the price. What about the **Zamberlan Men's 1996 VIOZ LUX GTX RR Leather Backpacking Boots**? What are the specific upgrades in those boots compared to the original best-selling model?
dialogue.agent: The **Zamberlan Men's 1996 VIOZ LUX GTX RR Leather Backpacking Boots** feature several upgrades compared to their best-selling original model. These boots have PU coated rubber rands for added durability, waxed Tuscan full-grain leather uppers with Hydrobloc treatment for water resistance, and Gore-Tex Performance Comfort membranes for waterproof and breathable protection. The outsole is a proprietary Zamberlan Vibram 3D with PU midsoles, designed for excellent grip and support. They also feature an improved Zamberlan Flex System for comfortable forward flex while maintaining lateral support, and high-resistance hardware that resists corrosion. These boots are crafted in Italy and have an average rating of 4.6/5 stars with 59 reviews.

top_reviews.title: Amazing boots
top_reviews.text:
I've never owned a serious pair of leather boots before, thinking them too heavy and uncomfortably warm/hot. I've always worn hiking shoes or synthetic boots - and still use them. But these boots have changed my mind. They are great backpacking boots that can also be used for hiking. They are comfortable, light and not any warmer than my synthetic boots. The foot and ankle support are amazing. I've never had better support in a boot. The boots can be pricey, but, I'm sure, they will last me for decades. I highly recommend them. As usual I order a 1/2 size larger than my standard shoe size.

9 months later, I want to add something to my review. I hike in the winter and have some winter hiking boots for snowy hikes when my boots will get very wet. This winter, the trails have been packed snow, so I wore my Zamberlans. The temperature on my last two hikes, when I got out of my pickup, was 5F. I hiked for 5 to 6 hours and my feet were nice and warm the whole time. Once again, great boots.

top_reviews.title: Manufacturing defect caused a blister. Zamberlan refused to fix.
top_reviews.text: This boot always causes a blister to my right heel because there is a manufacturing defect causing a bump in the heel wall. Zamberlan refused to address rather told me it was my fault for not lacing tight enough etc. I don't think this is true because this is my second pair and the first pair were outstanding I wore them out. Very disappointed with Zamberlan. The boots are a total $400 loss. I bought them for a Grand Canyon rim to rim hike. I cannot wear them.  I purchased Merrill boots with which I hiked the rim to rim three times.  Very little break in with the Merrill's . Outstanding boots. Don't waste your money on Zamberlan. Buy Merrill. Zamberlan doesn't take care of their customers. They used to be a good company but no longer.

top_reviews.title: Quality boot.
top_reviews.text:
I use these boots for work and not hiking. I do construction work, so I’m on my feet all day. These boots are made very well, that’s for sure. I’m a size 13 and they fit and feel perfect from the very first day. This is actually my third pair. I wear them year round. Not too hot in summer and not too cold in winter with some good socks. They stay waterproof for quite some time as well. The only downside is that the soles wear rather quick, but with me, it’s because I wear them every day of the work week.
I would still highly recommend these boots. Very well made and very comfortable.
I’m fortunate enough at the time to be able to spend the $345 on the boots. They seem pricey, but I honestly think they’re worth the cost.
I used to get the 996, but the 1996 are definitely a step up. The rubber rand really helps protecting the boot.

dialogue.user:
Those **Zamberlan Men's 1996 VIOZ LUX GTX RR Leather Backpacking Boots** sound very well-made and durable, which is exactly what I'm looking for. The Gore-Tex and the treated leather are great features, and the Vibram sole is a big plus for me. They are within my budget and meet my rating requirement. I think I'll go with those.
